candidates: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 - Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row.. `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for this topic. That can happen when the email came from a mention, a group or category notification, or mailing-list mode for a topic they never opened. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link returns a 500. Fix: handle the missing row, for example with `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row when it is missing. Using `TopicUser.change` also publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change event, which the direct `tu.save!` skips.

config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 - `unsubscribe_link` now needs `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which other senders do not pass.. MessageBuilder renders `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only the post notification path now passes `unsubscribe_url`. Other emails that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, such as the digest email, will hit a missing interpolation argument. That either raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email is not sent, or the email shows a literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` and a wrong "this particular topic" line. The spec had to add `unsubscribe_url` to keep passing, which shows the same failure. I did not see the digest call site itself. Fix: use a separate key for the topic sentence and add it only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 - A GET request changes notification state and lowers it again on every load.. The `unsubscribe` action is a plain GET with no CSRF token, and it changes persistent state. Any third-party page can add `` and mute topics for a logged-in visitor. Email link scanners and prefetchers will also trigger it. Each request also lowers the level one more step (watching → regular → muted), so reloading the page or loading it twice mutes a topic the user only meant to stop watching. Fix: render a confirmation page on GET and make the change on a POST/PUT with a CSRF token, or use a signed per-user token. At minimum, set a fixed target level so repeat requests change nothing.
